slides.title: The CIA dosed unwitting members of the public with LSD.
It began with a fear
slides.body: Korean War POWs gave confessions US officials read as 'brainwashing.' In 1953 CIA Director Allen Dulles launched MK-Ultra in response.

slides.title: 149 subprojects
slides.body: Drugs, hypnosis, sensory deprivation and electroshock, tested at universities, hospitals, prisons and military bases, funded through fronts.

slides.title: Behind one-way mirrors
slides.body: Subjects often didn't know they were being tested. LSD was given to unwitting members of the public, sometimes in safe houses with one-way mirrors.

slides.title: Frank Olson, 1953
slides.body: The biochemist was secretly dosed at a CIA retreat. Days later he fell from a 13th-floor hotel window. Ruled suicide; a 1994 exam raised serious questions.

slides.title: The files they missed
slides.body: In 1973 CIA Director Richard Helms ordered all MK-Ultra files destroyed. Financial records in a separate archive survived. In 1975 the Senate exposed it.

caption: Twenty years, 149 subprojects, unwitting test subjects, and no working mind control at the end of it. Which part is the most disturbing?
